_comment: ONE definition of the credential-redaction rule, imported by BOTH tools/redact/redact_captures.py
(the file tool) and tools/harness.ps1 (capture time). Neither side may carry its own copy.
safe_keys is an ALLOWLIST and starts EMPTY: every query-string value is redacted unless a key is
argued in here in review. controls is the near-miss corpus both engines must pass; every value
is synthetic (SYNTH-*) and no real value may ever be added. Rows whose expected equals input are

A serializer may write the separators escaped: & as \u0026 (PowerShell 5.1's ConvertTo-Json), as \U0026, or as &; = as \u003d; and // as \/\/. The patterns read all of those as the character they stand for, so a URI inside a JSON record is redacted past its first value and the detector is not blind to one - C28, C29, C31, C32, C33, C36.
param captures three groups: key, the separator it was written with, and the value. The separator is re-emitted verbatim so an escaped '=' survives the rewrite byte for byte.

The one shape no rule here can catch: a URI split across two strings or two lines. The orphan fragment carries no scheme, no host and no '?', and anything that claimed it would claim prose too (C07, C13, C14, C20). C39 and C40 state that limitation as controls so it stays a declared property.

controls.label: C01 scheme uri, two params
C02 upper-case key
C03 mixed-case key
C04 keys the tool never enumerates - the allowlist proving itself
C05 near-miss key: a blocklist on the substring 'password' would mangle this key
C06 innocuous key - proves this is not value-matching
C07 PROSE - the decisive over-redaction control, must be untouched
controls.input: the password is logged by the engine, not by us; password= appears in prose here
controls.expected: the password is logged by the engine, not by us; password= appears in prose here

controls.label: C08 uri with no query - host and verb must survive
C09 empty value beside a real one
C10 the engine's Peer line shape
C11 SCHEMELESS authority - the gap the first cut missed
C12 identifier in prose, outside any query string - untouched by design
C13 prose with a dot and a question mark - untouched

controls.expected: version 3.5? yes=maybe, but no host here

controls.label: C14 prose question - untouched
C15 idempotence - a second pass changes nothing
C16 CRLF survives byte-for-byte
C17 SCHEMELESS, MID-LINE, two params, tags before and verb after
C18 JSON BODY - a uri inside a JSON string value; the quotes and the rest of the object survive
C19 NEAR-MISS NEGATIVE: 'passwordless' in prose - untouched
controls.input: login is passwordless on this build
controls.expected: login is passwordless on this build

controls.label: C20 NEAR-MISS NEGATIVE: 'password_policy=' as a k=v in prose, no host - untouched
C21 NEAR-MISS NEGATIVE: 'discordid' inside a longer word in prose - untouched
controls.input: the discordidentity=SYNTH-21 label names this machine
controls.expected: the discordidentity=SYNTH-21 label names this machine

controls.label: C22 ...but inside a query string the allowlist redacts EVERY key, longer word or not
C23 the 2026-08-27 line shape, timestamped as the gamelog carries it, on the failed verb
C24 the census endpoint line - bracketed ip:port with no query - untouched
C25 a value that itself contains '=' is redacted whole
C26 two uris on one line - both redacted
C27 schemeless inside a JSON string
C28 JSON-ESCAPED separator: PowerShell 5.1 writes & as \u0026 inside JSON strings; every value after it must still go
C29 JSON-escaped separator on the schemeless form
C30 a backslash that is not the escaped separator ends the value; the tail is not a query
C31 HTML/XML-escaped separator: a writer that escapes & as & must not hide every value past the first
C32 UPPER-CASE JSON escape \U0026 - the same separator, the other spelling
C33 JSON-escaped scheme separator ws:\/\/ - the slashes a serializer escaped
C34 bracketed IPv6 authority with a query - a host form the dotted-label rule cannot see
C35 array-style key ids[] - a key class without brackets leaves the value in cleartext
C36 JSON-escaped '=' (\u003d): the separator is escaped, the value is not, and the escape survives the rewrite
C37 NEAR-MISS NEGATIVE: bracketed IPv6 with no query - the census line, untouched
C38 NEAR-MISS NEGATIVE: an array-style k=v in prose, no host - untouched
controls.input: ids[]=3 was read from the roster dump
controls.expected: ids[]=3 was read from the roster dump

controls.label: C39 DECLARED LIMITATION: a URI split across two JSON strings. The second fragment carries no scheme, no host and no '?', so no rule can claim it without also claiming prose (C07, C13, C14, C20). The first half IS redacted; the orphan is stated here so the blind spot is a recorded property of the rule rather than something an audit discovers.
C40 DECLARED LIMITATION: the same split across two lines - a value on a line of its own is prose to any rule that must leave prose alone
